subject: Future Tech
title: Printing Bone and Implants
description: A quick, practical guide to Printing Bone and Implants.

hook.text: Surgeons use 3D-printed titanium implants to replace damaged bones. Each implant is custom-fit to the patient's anatomy.

buildup.text: CT scans create a precise digital model of the defect. Engineers design an implant that fills the gap exactly.

discovery.text: Printed implants have a porous lattice that natural bone grows into, fusing the implant permanently to the body.

twist.text: Bioceramics can also be printed. These materials dissolve slowly, replaced by real bone as the patient heals.

climax.text: Over 100,000 patients have received 3D-printed orthopedic implants.

punchline.text: Every fracture is unique. Every implant should be too.
